title: Write docs/features/test-runs.md: the run model, guarantees kept from the launcher, tool API, wake contract, UI
outcome:
WHY FIRST: every other task cites one contract; reviewers check code against it.

HOW
1. New file docs/features/test-runs.md with sections: Model (TestRun record fields and states queued|running|passed|failed|unknown|canceled); Guarantees kept from the launcher (real exits only; unknown != pass; fingerprint before/after, drift = failure; first failure stops later stages, marked unrun; source/index unchanged during a run; hidden spawns; results.json + per-stage logs under Git's review-runs are the record of truth); Failure taxonomy (agent exit / TermAl host restart / OS reboot / terminal evidence vs wake delivery - see the epic comment from Codex #1846); Supervision and boot reconciliation; Admission (one run per worktree, execution.lock); Tool API (termal_start_test_run / get / list / cancel / wait); Wake contract (durable activation like a delegation wait; bounded summary shape; exactly once; Stop respected per tm-oixt); HTTP routes (list/get/cancel/rerun/stage log tail+follow); UI (Test Runs tab per the prototype linked on the epic); Retention (explicit prune, never running/unknown); Migration (hosted agents use the tool; CLI --detach --notify stays for external coordinators).
2. Cross-link both ways: docs/test.md (launcher section), docs/architecture.md (Work visualizer-style paragraph + route table rows), docs/features/agent-delegation-sessions.md (waits/fan-in), docs/features/agent-mailboxes.md (wake vs mailbox), docs/features/README.md index.
3. Reuse the exact wording of scripts/test-launcher.mjs guarantees (executeRun, summarize) rather than paraphrasing; cite tm-uex8 as the launcher adoption epic.
4. No code in this task. Reviewed by the epic owner before tm-ncc6.2 starts.

DEPENDS ON: nothing. BLOCKS: tm-ncc6.2 .. .10.

REVIEW FIXES (subagent review 2026-09-23, findings F1-F4, F5, F6, F10, F14, F17 - contract-level decisions live here)
- Section 'Supervision: restart survival' - DECISION FOR GREG. The terminal job object is created with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (src/terminal.rs:1025) and owned by TerminalProcessTree (657-659): when TermAl exits, Windows kills the whole run. Options: (A) keep kill-on-close - every TermAl restart makes the run unknown, no Windows re-attach; (B) a DEDICATED job for test runs without kill-on-close - cancel still TerminateJobObject; after restart re-attach by pid + creation-time identity (Windows: OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) and wait on the handle; Unix: setsid leader, liveness poll); cancel after re-attach is best effort for already-running grandchildren. PROPOSED: B (the motivating incident was a full gate killed by a TermAl restart). Write the chosen option and its consequences as normative text.
- Section 'Stop semantics' - DECISION FOR GREG. User Stop clears queued Orchestrator-source prompts (src/session_lifecycle.rs:541-551, 1062-1070 -> clear_queued_prompts_by_source src/session_interaction.rs:701-709) and consumes pending delegation waits with ParentSessionStopped (src/delegations.rs:2430-2450); the resume path queues via queue_orchestrator_prompt_on_record (delegations.rs:2569 -> session_interaction.rs:517-527). So 'the resume prompt stays queued until explicit resume' is NOT achievable with that path. Options: (i) mirror delegation waits fully: Stop consumes pending run waits (reason parentSessionStopped) and drops a queued run resume; the run record and the Test Runs tab keep the result; no automatic reactivation (consistent with tm-oixt); (ii) a new Stop-surviving QueuedPromptSource::TestRun (session_interaction.rs:144-149) with changes in dispatch_orphaned_workflow_prompts (turn_dispatch.rs:813-835), clear_queued_prompts_by_source*, Engram admission labels (engram_host_adapter.rs:6032-6034) and boot FIFO rules. PROPOSED: (i) for this slice.
- Section 'Host verdicts': canceled and unknown are HOST verdicts evidenced by a NON-terminal results.json (the launcher has no signal handler: a killed run leaves state running, the current stage running, later stages unrun, no ended; `summary` prints UNKNOWN). They are sticky across boot; the launcher's own terminal predicate (state in {passed,failed} and ended and integer exitCode, scripts/test-launcher.mjs:603-604) decides passed/failed.
- Section 'Why foreground mode': `_run` needs Node's IPC channel (process.send, launcher 702-705) and a JS-side createRun; a Rust host therefore spawns the foreground CLI (full|focused|live) as a hidden child and supervises it; detached mode/--notify stay for coordinators outside TermAl.
- Section 'Admission': execution.lock is per-run-directory, empty and never removed (launcher:415) - it is NOT a worktree lock and carries no pid. One run per root = no non-terminal host record for the root AND no disk-indexed results.json 'running' whose pid is alive with matching identity (a CLI-started run). A dead-pid running results.json is indexed unknown and never blocks.
- Section 'Identity': the host assigns run_id at spawn (state starting); the launcher's test-<uuid>, run dir and expected fingerprint are filled from the receipt (tm-uex8.12), which must be one flushed machine-parseable line printed before executeRun and even when fingerprint capture failed.
- Section 'Remote': start/cancel/rerun refuse remote-proxy sessions and projects with remote_id != LOCAL_REMOTE_ID with 501 (Phase 1, as delegations do at delegations.rs:505-510).
- Section 'Wake body': host header (state, reason, run dir, wait id, expected fingerprint, drift) + the launcher's summarize() text (captured stdout of the foreground run, or `summary RUN_DIR` in a hidden bounded read), overall cap 64 KiB (delegations.rs:45); never log bodies.
- Owner approval of this document is a process gate recorded as a comment, not an acceptance criterion.
acceptance:
- docs/features/test-runs.md exists with sections: Model, Guarantees kept from the launcher, Failure taxonomy (agent exit / TermAl restart / OS reboot / lost wake), Host verdicts, Supervision & restart survival (option A or B stated normatively), Stop semantics (option i or ii stated normatively), Admission, Identity, Tool API, Wake contract (body shape + 64 KiB cap), HTTP, UI, Retention, Remote, Migration.
- Every guarantee sentence cites the launcher behaviour (scripts/test-launcher.mjs line ranges) or is marked as a host addition.
- The failure taxonomy table gives, per case, the resulting run state, what results.json looks like and what the requester sees.
- Cross-links both ways with docs/test.md, docs/architecture.md, agent-delegation-sessions.md, agent-mailboxes.md, docs/features/README.md; no dangling links (checked by the docs link test if present, else by grep).
- The two decisions (restart survival, Stop) are recorded with Greg's choice before tm-ncc6.2 starts (comment on this task).
